skill.name: deep-research
skill.description: Research assistant for synthesizing multi-source information, evaluating credibility, and producing structured summaries with citations.
skill.summary: Synthesizes sources into cited research briefs with findings, debates, and gaps.
skill.author: shubhamsaboo

content.value_statement: Deep research is hard when sources disagree or lack context. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to synthesize sources, compare viewpoints, and produce cited research summaries.
actual_capabilities: Clarifies research questions before gathering information.
Breaks topics into subtopics and main questions.
Evaluates source credibility and publication currency.
Synthesizes findings into executive summaries and detailed analysis.
Organizes citations, consensus, debate, gaps, and further research.
limitations: It does not fetch sources unless the host agent has browsing or retrieval tools.
It relies on the model to verify citations and avoid unsupported claims.
It is not a substitute for expert legal, medical, or financial advice.
Example citations should be verified before external use.

use_cases.title: Prepare Policy Briefs
use_cases.description: Compare official reports, expert commentary, and news coverage to summarize risks, tradeoffs, and open questions.

use_cases.title: Analyze Market Topics
use_cases.description: Turn scattered source material into a structured brief with trends, competing views, and research gaps.

use_cases.title: Draft Literature Summaries
use_cases.description: Organize academic and secondary sources into key findings, citations, and areas for further investigation.

prompt_templates.title: Research a Topic
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a structured overview.
prompt_templates.prompt: Research [topic]. Clarify the main question, identify key aspects, and summarize the strongest findings with citations.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Viewpoints
prompt_templates.prompt: Research [topic] from multiple perspectives. Separate areas of consensus, areas of debate, and claims that need stronger evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate Sources
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request focused on source quality.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these sources about [topic]. Rank their credibility, note publication dates, identify bias risks, and explain which claims each source supports.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Evidence Brief
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an evidence brief on [topic] for [audience]. Include an executive summary, key findings, detailed analysis, citations, limitations, and further research needs.

output_examples.input: Research the benefits and risks of intermittent fasting.
output_examples.output: The skill returns an executive summary, key findings, detailed analysis, consensus points, debates, cited sources, and research gaps.

output_examples.input: Compare expert views on remote work productivity.
output_examples.output: The skill separates agreement, disagreement, evidence quality, source credibility, and practical implications for different organizations.

output_examples.input: Evaluate sources for a report on battery recycling.
output_examples.output: The skill highlights authoritative reports, notes weak or outdated sources, and maps each source to supported claims.

best_practices: State the research question, audience, and desired depth before starting.
Ask for source credibility notes when the topic affects decisions.
Verify citations and dates before publishing or sharing the output.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for a conclusion before the evidence is reviewed.
Do not treat generated citations as verified without checking them.
Do not use this skill as professional advice for regulated decisions.

faq.question: What does this skill produce?
faq.answer: It produces structured research summaries with key findings, detailed analysis, citations, debate areas, and research gaps.

faq.question: Does it browse the web by itself?
faq.answer: No. It needs the host agent to provide browsing, retrieval, or source material.

faq.question: Can it evaluate source quality?
faq.answer: Yes. It prompts the agent to consider credibility, publication dates, source type, and uncertainty.

faq.question: Is it useful for academic work?
faq.answer: Yes, but users should verify all citations and follow their institution rules.

faq.question: Can it compare conflicting viewpoints?
faq.answer: Yes. It explicitly separates consensus, debate, uncertainty, and gaps.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
